Even a few seconds of public visibility on the archive would seed GitHub's search index with that material, and the flip-back doesn't unindex it. (A1) trades a permanent risk for a transient board-UI tidy. (A2) defeats the portfolio's whole point during the window. (A3) loses the multi-agent claim-comment history. **(A4) gets the operational win** (skills/helpers no longer trip on the legacy URLs) **without touching visibility**.

If you want a longer-term plan, file a `#XX archive→public migration after history-scrub` ticket once `#13` lands — then (A1) becomes viable because the archive history would also be sanitized.

(That's the union of 9 issues, with #53 being a heavy cross-referencer.)

## Options for the boss

(R1) **Rewrite the new bodies** to remap each `#N` to its new ai-harness#M using the map. For refs to closed-and-not-migrated archive items (#1, #2, #3, #8, #23), rewrite as the full archive URL — `jdtogni78/ai-harness-archive#N` — which renders as a clickable cross-repo ref. ~9 edits, mechanical, I can script it. Cleanest reader experience, no map-consultation needed.

(R2) **Annotate, don't rewrite.** Append a one-line note to each affected new body:
     > Note: `#N` references in the body above use the legacy archive numbering — see [`docs/board-issue-transfer-map.md`](…).
     Lighter touch, preserves the original verbatim wording, but every reader has to translate via the map.

(R3) **Do nothing in the bodies**, document the gotcha only in the map file header. Cheapest, but the issue bodies themselves silently mislead. The boss's framing — "the map file is the only forward-link" — gestures this way.

(R4) **R1 for the heavy cross-referencer (#53)**, R2 for the rest. #53 alone has 12 stale refs and is the worst single offender; the others have 1-2 each.

I'd lean (R1) — the cost is small (~9 issues, scriptable from the map I already have in memory) and it removes a foot-gun that lives forever in the new issue bodies. (R3) leaves landmines.
